# AI contributions

Tenpai is a school project. Every file or block of code written by Claude
(Anthropic, via Claude Code) is marked in place and listed here, so a grader can
tell at a glance what the student wrote and what the AI wrote. Student-authored
code carries no marker.

## Marker convention

Checked by `dart run tool/check_conventions.dart`. The token is `AI-GENERATED`.

**Whole file** — one header within the first 15 lines (after YAML front matter
or an H1 when the format requires it), using the file's comment syntax:

```dart
// AI-GENERATED by Claude (Claude Code), 2026-09-17
// Why: one line, only when the author asked for one.
```

```python
# AI-GENERATED by Claude (Claude Code), 2026-09-17
```

```markdown
<!-- AI-GENERATED by Claude (Claude Code), 2026-09-17 -->
```

**Block inside a student-authored file** — a BEGIN line naming the block and a
matching END line, same comment syntax, never nested:

```kotlin
// AI-GENERATED (Claude) BEGIN — INTERNET permission
...
// AI-GENERATED (Claude) END
```

Rules:

- Date is the day the content was written, ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`.
- The optional `Why:` line goes directly under the header or BEGIN line.
  Claude asks the author once per task whether why-lines are wanted; it does
  not invent reasons.
- Files that cannot hold comments (JSON, binaries) are listed below with
  scope `file (no marker)`.
- Every file with a header marker must appear in the table below; every path
  in the table must exist. The checker enforces both.
- Under `/implement`, anything Claude writes into `lib/` gets a header (new
  file) or BEGIN/END (edit) before the turn ends.
